questions.stem: What is an accrual in accounting?

options.text: An expense incurred but not yet paid

questions.explanation: An accrual is an expense that has been incurred but not yet paid. It is recorded to ensure expenses are matched to the period they relate to.

distractorRationale.a: This describes a prepayment, not an accrual.
distractorRationale.b: This is income received in advance, not an accrual.
distractorRationale.d: This describes income that has been fully realized, not an accrual.

questions.stem: How should prepayments be recorded in the balance sheet?
questions.explanation: Prepayments are recorded as assets because they represent expenses that have been paid in advance for future periods.

distractorRationale.a: Liabilities represent amounts owed, not prepayments.
distractorRationale.c: Expenses are costs incurred, not prepayments.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a prepayment?

options.text: Rent paid for the next year
Salary owed but not yet paid
Interest received but not yet earned

questions.explanation: Rent paid for the next year is a prepayment because it is an expense paid in advance.

distractorRationale.a: This is an accrual, not a prepayment.
distractorRationale.c: This is an accrual, not a prepayment.
distractorRationale.d: This is income received in advance, not a prepayment.

questions.stem: A business has an unpaid electricity bill of ₦50,000 at year-end. How should this be recorded?
questions.explanation: An unpaid electricity bill is an accrual and should be recorded as a liability because it represents an expense incurred but not yet paid.

distractorRationale.a: Prepayments are expenses paid in advance, not unpaid bills.
distractorRationale.b: Assets represent resources owned, not unpaid expenses.
distractorRationale.d: Income represents earnings, not unpaid expenses.
